title: Staged Activation Chronograph and KPI Compass
body:
Purpose:
A compact, time-forward tracker (chronograph) paired with a KPI compass to guide a staged rollout for platform features that touch inference routing, Dedicated capacity, and Console rollouts. This doc is intentionally lightweight — meant for daily standups during the 4-week activation window and to be the single source of truth for telemetry owners and on-call leads.

Scope:
- Applies to small-to-medium staged rollouts (10k–500k monthly active requests) for Hosted API changes and Dedicated scheduling tweaks.
- NOT for infra-only kernel upgrades that require extended SRE-led maintenance (those get a separate runbook).

High-level rollout tempo (chronograph):
- Week 0 (Prep): config freeze window, smoke tests on staging, owner sign-offs.
- Week 1 (Canary): 1% traffic, 2-day observation. Validate latency P50/P95 and error budget.
- Week 2 (Ramp): 5% -> 20% over 3 days with automated pause windows.
- Week 3 (Scale): 50% -> 100% across regions with Dedicated pool growth if needed.
- Week 4 (Stabilize): Post-ramp checks, quality evaluation against eval sets, and metrics handoff.

Primary KPIs (KPI Compass) — owners and measurement queries: (owners listed)
- End-to-end latency (P50/P95/P99) — owner: Marco Ruiz — query: looker:redwood.api_latency_by_route (daily)
- Token cost per request (avg cpu/gpu token-cost) — owner: Aisha Patel — query: bigquery:billing.token_cost_agg (hourly)
- Error rate (5xx and model-fallbacks) — owner: Leah Kim — query: grafana:redwood.errors.total (1m)
- Quality drift (eval-set BLEU/ROUGE/LLR) — owner: Maya Chen — evals repo link in linked artifacts (daily)
- Cache hit ratio (prefix/KV) — owner: infra-sre@example.com — monitoring dashboard: cache-hits-dashboard

Go / No-go decision criteria (canary -> ramp):
- Go: P95 latency within +10% of baseline AND error rate < 0.5% AND cost delta within budgeted +/-5%
- No-go: repeated model fallbacks > 3 within a 30m window OR user-facing error rate > 1.5% OR model-quality regression detected on golden prompt set

Preflight checklist (tick boxes for standup):
[ ] Owner alignments done (product, eng, infra, SRE, support)
[ ] Smoke tests: generation, embeddings, reranking on staging
[ ] Canary routing configured with automated rollback hook
[ ] Rate limits and quotas reviewed for canary cohort
[ ] Cost cap set for canary cohort and alerting enabled
[ ] CORS and auth integration sanity checks complete
[ ] Customer-facing comms draft (if any external beta) prepared by CS

Traffic ramp / capacity plan snapshot:
- Canary (1% global) — target vCPU/GPU: current pool; no autoscale needed
- 5% -> 20%: enable burst autoscaling up to +30% of Dedicated pool; monitor queue lengths and batching latencies
- >50%: provision additional Dedicated nodes (order id: infra-cap-2024-77) — infra lead: Daniel O'Connor

Runbook snippets (quick actions):
- If P95 rises >30% and sustained 10m: reduce canary traffic by 50% and open incident channel (#launch-incident)
- If error rate spikes with model fallbacks: switch to fallback model variant and notify ML model owner; gather example requests for postmortem
- If cost delta > +20% sustained for 1 hour: pause ramp, notify finance owner and product ops to evaluate config changes (quantization / batch size)

Communication & escalation matrix:
- Primary channel: #prodops-rollouts (Slack) — product ops lead monitors
- Incident channel: #launch-incident — SRE, infra, and product on-call required within 15 minutes
- External comms: CS drafted template (linked in linked_artifacts) — product ops approves

Monitoring & dashboard checklist for daily standups:
- Live dashboard: latency, errors, cost-per-token, cache-hit, traffic split by variant
- Alerting: P95 latency above threshold, error rate, cost burn rate — ensure alert routing points to on-call

Quality validation steps during rollout:
- Run golden prompt set nightly to check for quality regressions (owner: Maya Chen)
- Sampling: capture 0.5% of real requests for manual review (PII redaction enabled)
- Compare new variant outputs to baseline with automated diffs and human review if delta > threshold

Open questions / known risks (notes to self):
- Should we include regional stagger (APAC one day after NA) to reduce cross-region fallout? (needs legal + infra input)
- Unknown: impact of new batching strategy on short-tail queries — run micro-benchmarks before ramp
- Customer exposure: two enterprise customers have integrations that could surface errors; coordinate with solutions engineering for a private beta flag

Action items (owners):
- Marco: finalize P95 alert thresholds and runbook snippets — due 2024-11-08
- Aisha: produce cost probe simulations for 1%/5%/20% traffic — due 2024-11-09
- Daniel: verify Dedicated pool autoscale caps and confirm provisioning lead time — due 2024-11-11
- Leah: finalize comms and confirm support rotation for Week 1-3 — due 2024-11-07

Retro prompts (post-launch):
- Was the KPI compass adequate? Which metrics were noisy/insufficient?
- What early signals were most predictive of later issues?
- Cost vs. quality tradeoffs: did we hit expected unit economics?

Notes / quick references (informal):
- Slack threads: #feature-rollout-42 (contains dry run logs)
- GitHub PR: infra/pull/721 contains the canary routing change
- Confluence playbook has historical runbooks and incident templates

This doc is intended to be copied to the release channel and amended daily during ramp. Keep it light, highlight blockers at the top of the doc for standup.

-- Leah K.
